claims: Psilocybin is a naturally occurring compound found in over 100 species of fungi.
According to the RAND Corporation, psilocybin mushrooms are currently the most widely used psychedelic among U.S. adults.
LSD is a potent synthetic psychedelic derived from a rye fungus.
LSD is known as "acid".
LSD produces long-lasting effects up to 12 hours.
LSD is the prototypical classic psychedelic.
DMT is the active ingredient in the Amazonian brew Ayahuasca.
When inhaled, DMT's effects last 5–20 minutes.
Mescaline is found in Peyote.
Mescaline is found in San Pedro.
MDMA is classified primarily as an entactogen.
MDMA has mild psychedelic properties.
Ketamine is a "dissociative" anesthetic.
Ketamine can produce psychedelic effects at sub-anesthetic doses.
Esketamine is FDA-approved for treatment-resistant depression.
Research from April 2026 suggests psychedelics create a shared "neural fingerprint" by increasing "cross-talk" between brain systems that normally operate independently.
Most classic psychedelics (LSD, psilocybin, DMT) work by agonizing serotonin 5-HT2A receptors in the prefrontal cortex.
Psychedelics temporarily disrupt the Default Mode Network (DMN).
Psilocybin has shown substantial and sustained antidepressant effects, sometimes lasting up to a year after just two doses.
The FDA has designated MDMA as a "Breakthrough Therapy" for the treatment of post-traumatic stress disorder.
In the United States, most psychedelics remain Schedule I substances.
On April 18, 2026, an executive order was signed to speed up the review of certain psychedelics, including ibogaine, for medical use.
Oregon has legalized supervised psilocybin therapy.
Colorado has legalized supervised psilocybin therapy.
The United Nations classifies many psychedelics as high-risk.
Hallucinogen Persisting Perception Disorder (HPPD) is a rare condition that can cause "flashbacks" or visual disturbances long after the drug has left the system.
